questions.stem: An Intern gave Lignocaine plus adrenaline for suturing a cut wound on the forearm. He sutured it quickly and wanted to shorten the duration of soft-tissue anesthesia. Which of the following is FDA approved drug to reverse or shorten the duration of soft-tissue anesthesia when Sympathomimetics is used with local anesthetics?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phentolamine
  • Phentolamine is a reversible nonselective α-adrenergic antagonist. Its primary action is vasodilation due to α1 blockade. Non-selective α-blockers can cause a much more pronounced reflex tachycardia than selective α1 blockers.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 12th Edition, Page Number: 310

questions.stem: A 62-year-old male had BPH and his BP is 150/90mm of Hg. Which is the Best drug for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alfuzosin
  • Alfuzosin is a selective α1 antagonist used forhypertension with BPH because it blocks alpha 1 on blood vessels and prostatic urethra.
  • So a single drug can manage bothBPH and hypertension


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 523

questions.stem: A 22-year-old female had a scorpion bite and developed pulmonary odema and BP 190/110 mm of Hg. The best drug to manage this patient is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prazosin

Scorpion Bite

  • Scorpion bite leads to activation of autonomic hyperactivity
  • Excess catecholamines release causes hypertension and prazosin decreases it through its alpha-antagonistic action
  • In case of pulmonary edema and HTNin scorpion stings best drug is prazosin


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 523

questions.stem: The patient was taken for cataract surgery and developed floppy iris syndrome. On asking he revealed that he is also taking a drug for BPH. What drug patient was taking?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tamsulosin
  • Tamsulosin
    • Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome is characterized by a triad of flaccid iris stroma that undulates and billows in response to intraocular fluid currents, a propensity for the floppy iris stroma to prolapse toward the phacoemulsification and side-port incisions despite proper wound construction, and progressive intraoperative pupil constriction despite standard preventive preoperative pharmacologic measures
    • It is seen with tamsulosin, so need to take drug history before cataract surgery


Lange Katzung, Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 160

questions.stem: A 45-YEAR-old male patient with erectile dysfunction was given an Intracavernous injection of Phentolamine. All the following adverse effects are possible except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Impaired ejaculation
  • Direct intracavernous injection of Phentolamine in combination with papaverine has been proposed as a treatment for male sexual dysfunction
  • Intracavernous injection of Phentolamine may cause
    • Orthostatic hypotension
    • Priapism
    • Repetitive intra-penile injections may cause fibrotic reactions
    • Impaired ejaculation is not a known ADR


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 12th Edition, Page Number: 310

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male had Frequent or urgent need to urinate, Increased frequency of urination at night (nocturia), Difficulty starting urination, Weak urine stream or a stream that stops and starts, and Dribbling at the end of urination and give an alpha-blocker drug. Which is the best drug to prescribe to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tamsulosin
  • Tamsulosin is a selective α 1A receptor antagonist and acts mainly on the prostate without affecting alpha receptor subtypes in blood vessels.
  • So the patient will not have hypotension. But other drugs like Prazosin, doxazosin, and tolazoline are non-selective and block alpha 1A and alpha 1B and may cause hypotension in this elderly patient, so better avoid.


Lange Katzung, Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 160

questions.stem: Reflex bradycardia caused by Alpha-1 agonists can be blocked by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Atropine
  • Atropine is an anticholinergic which causes tachycardia, so this can be used in Reflex bradycardia caused by Alpha-1 agonists
  • Metoprolol is a cardio-selective beta blocker, which causes bradycardia
  • Mirtazapine is an atypical antidepressant and blocks α2 auto receptor
  • Phenylephrine is an alpha agonist, so no action on the heart


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 127

questions.stem: Midodrine is used in which of the following condition
questions.solutionHtml:
Orthostatic hypotension
  • Midodrine is a selective alpha-1 receptor antagonist used in the treatment of orthostatic hypotension
  • It increases upright blood pressure and improves orthostatic tolerance
  • After the oral dose, peak concentration achieved in one hour


Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 15th Edition, chapter 9, Page Number: 18,28

questions.stem: The drug used as an antismoking agent is
questions.solutionHtml:
Varenicline
  • Varenicline is a partial agonist at α4β2 receptors nicotinic receptor
  • This type of nicotinic receptor subtype is involved in nicotine addiction
  • Used as an antismoking agent
  • FDA has given a warning on CVS risk and increased suicidal risk

questions.stem: The following statements are true regarding carvedilol except:

options.label: B
options.text: No dose adjustment in renal failure

options.label: D
options.text: α1, β1 blockade and with agonistic activity at β2

questions.answerText: α1, β1 blockade and with agonistic activity at β2
questions.solutionHtml:
α1, β1 blockade and with agonistic activity at β2
  • Carvedilol - α1, β1 & β2 antagonist
  • Inhibits free radical-induced lipid peroxidation
  • Blocks L-type voltage-gated Calcium channels
  • Decreases vascular smooth muscle mitogenesis
  • Bioavailability is 25% to 35% due to a significant degree of first-pass metabolism
  • No dose adjustment in renal failure as it is metabolized in the liver
  • The metabolites of carvedilol are excreted primarily via the bile into the feces.


Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 15th Edition, chapter 10, Page Number: 13,21
